controller.connectionLost: Connection lost. Trying to get back…
controller.motionDenied: Motion access was denied. Allow it in your browser settings and reload.
controller.motionUnsupported: This device has no motion sensors.

broadcast.name: BroadcastChannel (same device)
broadcast.summary: Tabs and windows of one browser on one machine talk directly. No network, no server.
pros: Zero setup, zero cost, works offline
Great for local demos and tests
cons: Same browser profile on one machine only: phones cannot join

partykit.name: PartyKit (Cloudflare relay)
partykit.summary: A small WebSocket relay room on Cloudflare (PartyKit / Durable Objects). Phones and screens anywhere on the internet.
pros: Works across networks and NATs (it is a server)
Scales to hundreds of peers per room
Simple deploy: `npx partykit deploy` with examples/partykit/server.ts
cons: One relay hop of latency (usually 20–80 ms)
Host-authoritative: anyone with the code can ask to join unless you add `admit`
partykit.cost: Cloudflare has a free tier (Workers Free with daily request limits; Durable Objects allowances); the paid Workers plan starts at about $5/month. Check current Cloudflare pricing.

webrtc.name: WebRTC DataChannel (P2P)
webrtc.summary: Each guest opens a direct DataChannel to the host; a messaging transport (PartyKit) only carries the handshake.
pros: Lowest network latency between devices (often on the same LAN)
Room traffic never touches a server after the handshake
Auto-reconnect and large-message chunking built in
cons: Some networks need a TURN server
Star topology: the host's device relays everything, so keep rooms small (≈2–16)
webrtc.cost: P2P traffic is free; signaling uses the PartyKit free tier; the default public STUN server is free. TURN relays (Cloudflare, Twilio, self-hosted coturn) are billed per GB.

firebase.name: Firebase Realtime Database (managed)
firebase.summary: Google-managed backend: Cloud Functions admit peers atomically, security rules gate reads and writes, RTDB syncs state and presence.
pros: Server-authoritative join and capacity (up to 300 per room)
Managed: no server code to operate
cons: No ephemeral messaging yet: shared state only, so not for high-frequency input
Cloud Functions need the Blaze plan (credit card)
firebase.cost: Spark (free): 1 GB stored, 10 GB/month download, 100 simultaneous connections, no Cloud Functions. Blaze (pay-as-you-go, card required) includes free monthly quotas and is needed for Functions.

qr.name: QR code
qr.description: The host shows a QR code with the join URL; phones scan it.

code.name: Room code
code.description: A six-character code like ABC 234, typed on the guest device.

pin.name: Numeric PIN
pin.description: A six-digit PIN, easy to read aloud (relay transports only).

broadcast.name: Same-device broadcast
broadcast.description: Other tabs on the same machine find the room by code; no scanning.

same-device.name: Same device
same-device.description: Several tabs/windows/displays driven by one computer.

realtime.name: LAN / online realtime
realtime.description: Phones and screens anywhere, through a relay server.

p2p.name: P2P low latency
p2p.description: Direct device-to-device channels for fast input.

managed.name: Serverless managed
managed.description: A managed backend with server-side admission and persistence.

firebase.name: I already use Firebase
firebase.description: Reuse your Firebase project (Auth + RTDB + Functions).

cloudflare.name: Cloudflare / PartyKit
cloudflare.description: Deploy a tiny relay on Cloudflare.

none.name: No backend
none.description: Nothing to deploy; same machine (or P2P once you add signaling).
